sections.title: 3. Introduction
sections.body:
### 3.1 Purpose
This Business Requirements Document (BRD) defines the business needs, scope, and functional requirements for the development of a comprehensive Human Resources Management System (HRMS). The system is designed as a full-stack web and mobile application to streamline HR operations, employee lifecycle management, payroll, and recruitment processes.

### 3.2 Project Background
The organization requires a centralized, scalable, and secure platform to manage its workforce. The current need is for a production-ready system that supports multiple user roles (Super Admin, HR/Admin, Manager, Recruiter, Employee, Finance/Payroll) and integrates various HR modules including attendance, leave, payroll, recruitment, and performance management.

### 3.3 Business Problem
Manual or fragmented HR processes lead to inefficiencies, lack of visibility into workforce data, and compliance risks. The business needs a unified system to automate workflows, ensure data integrity, provide real-time analytics, and support regulatory compliance (including banking sector standards like SOX and ISO 27001).

### 3.4 Business Objectives
| ID | Objective | Success Measure |
|---|---|---|
| BO-01 | Centralize HR data management | 100% of employee master data migrated and accessible via single platform |
| BO-02 | Automate HR workflows | Reduction of manual processing time for onboarding/offboarding by 50% |
| BO-03 | Ensure regulatory compliance | Full audit trail and RBAC implementation meeting ISO 27001 and SOX standards |
| BO-04 | Enhance employee self-service | 90% of routine HR requests handled via self-service portal |

### 3.5 Expected Business Benefits
- Improved operational efficiency through automated workflows.
- Enhanced data accuracy and integrity via centralized master data management.
- Better decision-making through comprehensive HR analytics and dashboards.
- Increased employee satisfaction via self-service capabilities and transparent processes.
- Reduced compliance risk through robust audit logs and role-based access control.

sections.title: 4. Scope
sections.body:
### 4.1 In Scope
- Full-stack web and mobile application (Android, iOS) development.
- Role-based access control (RBAC) for Super Admin, HR/Admin, Manager, Recruiter, Employee, and Finance/Payroll users.
- Modules: Employee master data, onboarding/offboarding, attendance, leave management, payroll, recruitment, performance management, training, asset management, and expense management.
- Secure authentication, JWT/session management, and MFA-ready architecture.
- Integration with email/SMS/push notifications, calendar, and external APIs.
- Comprehensive dashboards, reports, and audit logs.

### 4.2 Out of Scope
- Payroll tax calculation engine (assumed to be handled by external tax service or manual input).
- Biometric attendance hardware integration (unless specified in future phases).
- Third-party ERP integration (beyond defined API integrations).

### 4.3 System Boundaries
The system will operate as a centralized backend API with a relational database, file/document storage, and notification service. It will interact with external systems via APIs for notifications, calendar integration, and potential payroll processing. The system will be hosted in a secure cloud environment with encryption and backup capabilities.

sections.title: 7. Business Process Overview
sections.body:
### 7.1 AS-IS Process
Currently, HR processes are managed through disparate tools and manual workflows, leading to data silos, lack of real-time visibility, and increased compliance risks.

### 7.2 TO-BE Process
The TO-BE process involves a centralized HRMS that automates workflows from recruitment to offboarding. Key workflows include:
- Recruitment → Candidate Selection → Offer → Joining → Onboarding
- Employee → Attendance/Leave → Payroll → Performance → Promotion/Transfer → Offboarding/Exit

### 7.3 Process Flow Narrative Description
The system will support configurable approval chains for HR, managers, finance, and admins. For example, a leave request initiated by an employee will be routed to their manager for approval, then to HR for final processing. Payroll processing will involve finance validating deductions and bonuses before generating payslips. All actions will be logged in audit trails for compliance.

sections.title: 9. Functional Requirements
sections.body:
### Module: Authentication & Access Control
- **FR-001**: Implement JWT/session-based authentication.
  - *Description*: Users authenticate via username/password, and sessions are managed using JWT.
  - *Preconditions*: User account exists and is active.
  - *Input*: Username, password.
  - *Processing*: Validate credentials, generate JWT token.
  - *Output*: Authenticated session with role-based permissions.
  - *Business Rules*: Passwords must meet complexity policies; MFA can be enforced for sensitive roles.
  - *Acceptance Criteria*: Given a valid user, when they log in, then they receive a JWT token and access to permitted modules.

### Module: Employee Master Data
- **FR-002**: Manage employee profiles, departments, designations, and branches.
  - *Description*: Centralized storage and management of employee data.
  - *Preconditions*: HR/Admin role.
  - *Input*: Employee details, department, designation, branch.
  - *Processing*: Validate and store data.
  - *Output*: Updated employee record.
  - *Business Rules*: Employee ID must be unique; department and designation must exist in master data.
  - *Acceptance Criteria*: Given an HR/Admin, when they update an employee's department, then the change is reflected in all related modules.

### Module: Attendance & Leave
- **FR-003**: Record attendance and manage leave requests.
  - *Description*: Employees log attendance; managers approve leave requests.
  - *Preconditions*: Employee and manager accounts exist.
  - *Input*: Attendance logs, leave requests.
  - *Processing*: Validate leave balance, route for approval.
  - *Output*: Approved/rejected leave, updated attendance records.
  - *Business Rules*: Leave balance cannot be negative; approvals follow configured workflows.
  - *Acceptance Criteria*: Given an employee, when they submit a leave request, then it is routed to their manager for approval.

### Module: Payroll
- **FR-004**: Process payroll with deductions, bonuses, and tax compliance.
  - *Description*: Calculate salaries, apply deductions, and generate payslips.
  - *Preconditions*: Employee data and salary structures are configured.
  - *Input*: Salary structures, deductions, bonuses.
  - *Processing*: Calculate net pay, apply tax rules.
  - *Output*: Payslips, payroll summaries.
  - *Business Rules*: Tax calculations must comply with statutory requirements; payslips are immutable once generated.
  - *Acceptance Criteria*: Given a payroll cycle, when it is processed, then accurate payslips are generated for all employees.

sections.title: 10. Non-Functional Requirements
sections.body:
### 10.1 Performance
- System must support 1,000 concurrent users with response times < 2 seconds for standard operations.
- Payroll processing for 10,000 employees must complete within 1 hour.

### 10.2 Security
- Implement RBAC, JWT/session management, and MFA-ready architecture.
- Encrypt data at rest and in transit (AES-256, TLS 1.3).
- Maintain immutable audit logs for all critical actions (per ISO 27001).

### 10.3 Availability
- System must achieve 99.99% uptime (per banking domain benchmarks).
- Implement failover and disaster recovery mechanisms.

### 10.4 Scalability
- Support horizontal scaling for web and API layers.
- Database must handle 10x growth in employee records without performance degradation.

### 10.5 Usability
- Modern, responsive UI for web, Android, and iOS.
- Intuitive navigation with search, filters, and pagination.

### 10.6 Maintainability
- Modular architecture with clear separation of concerns.
- Comprehensive logging and monitoring for troubleshooting.

### 10.7 Compatibility
- Support modern browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge).
- Compatible with Android 10+ and iOS 14+.

sections.title: 11. Business Rules
table: Each employee must have a unique identifier across the system.
Employees cannot request leave exceeding their available balance.
Generated payslips cannot be modified after approval.
Users can only access modules and data permitted by their role.
All critical actions (e.g., payroll processing, data deletion) must be logged.
MFA can be enforced for sensitive roles (e.g., Super Admin, Finance/Payroll).

sections.title: 12. Data Requirements
sections.body:
### 12.1 Data Entities
- Employee
- Department
- Designation
- Branch
- Attendance
- Leave Request
- Payroll Record
- Payslip
- Job Posting
- Candidate
- Performance Review

### 12.2 Data Fields
| Entity | Field | Data Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Employee | Employee ID | String | Yes | Unique identifier |
| Employee | Name | String | Yes | Full name |
| Employee | Department ID | String | Yes | Foreign key to Department |
| Attendance | Date | Date | Yes | Date of attendance |
| Attendance | Status | Enum | Yes | Present, Absent, Late |
| Payroll Record | Employee ID | String | Yes | Foreign key to Employee |
| Payroll Record | Net Pay | Decimal | Yes | Calculated net salary |

### 12.3 Data Validation
- Employee ID must be unique.
- Dates must be in valid format.
- Monetary values must be non-negative.

### 12.4 Data Retention
- Employee records retained for 7 years post-offboarding (per SOX).
- Audit logs retained for 5 years (per ISO 27001).

sections.title: 14. Interface Requirements
sections.body:
### 14.1 User Interface
- Responsive web UI with modern design.
- Mobile apps for Android and iOS.
- Dashboards with charts, tables, and filters.

### 14.2 API Interface
- RESTful API with JSON payloads.
- JWT-based authentication.
- Rate limiting and error handling.

### 14.3 Hardware Interface
- No specific hardware requirements beyond standard servers and client devices.

sections.title: 15. Security Requirements
table: Implement RBAC for all user roles
Encrypt data at rest and in transit

sections.title: 18. Assumptions and Dependencies
sections.body:
### Assumptions
- Users have stable internet access for web and mobile apps.
- External services (email, SMS, calendar) are reliable and available.
- Master data (departments, designations) is maintained by HR/Admin.

### Dependencies
- Integration with external tax service for statutory compliance.
- Availability of cloud infrastructure for hosting.
- Stakeholder input for workflow configuration.

sections.title: 19. Constraints
sections.body:
- **Budget**: Not specified in source document — pending stakeholder input.
- **Timeline**: Not specified in source document — pending stakeholder input.
- **Technology**: Must use relational database, RESTful API, and modern web/mobile frameworks.
- **Regulatory**: Must comply with PCI-DSS, SOX, AML/KYC, and ISO 27001.
- **Team**: Assumed to have full-stack developers, QA engineers, and DevOps specialists.
- **Infrastructure**: Cloud-based hosting with encryption and backup capabilities.

sections.title: 20. Risks
table: Data breach due to inadequate security

sections.title: 21. Acceptance Criteria
sections.body:
The system will be accepted when:
1. All functional requirements (FR-001 to FR-004) are implemented and tested.
2. Security requirements (SEC-001 to SEC-006) are verified.
3. Non-functional requirements (performance, availability, scalability) are met.
4. User acceptance testing (UAT) is completed with no critical defects.
5. Documentation (BRD, SRS, API docs, RTM) is finalized.

File: HR Management System.pdf

HR Management System 
 
Build a complete HR Management System (HRMS) as a full-stack web and mobile 
application with role-based access for Super Admin, HR/Admin, Manager, Recruiter, 
Employee, and Finance/Payroll users. The system should include **secure authentication, 
role and permission management, employee master data, departments, designations, branches, 
employee onboarding/offboarding, employee profiles, document management, attendance, 
shift and roster management, leave and holiday management, work-from-home/remote-work 
requests, regularization, timesheets, payroll, salary structures, deductions, bonuses, 
reimbursements, payslips, tax/statutory information, recruitment and applicant tracking, job 
postings, candidate pipeline, interviews, offers, joining management, performance 
management, goals/KPIs, appraisals, feedback, training and learning, asset management, 
employee grievances, announcements, notifications, company policies, HR letters/certificates, 
expense management, travel requests, approval workflows, surveys, employee self-service, 
manager self-service, and comprehensive dashboards and reports. Include search, filters, 
sorting, pagination, bulk import/export, Excel/CSV upload, PDF generation, audit logs, 
activity history, configurable workflows, email/SMS/push notifications, reminders, 
calendar integration, and API integrations. The dashboard should provide HR analytics 
such as headcount, attendance, leave utilization, attrition, recruitment status, payroll 
summaries, department statistics, performance, pending approvals, and upcoming events. 
The project should have a modern responsive UI for Web, Android, and iOS, with a 
centralized backend API, relational database, file/document storage, notification service, 
background jobs, logging, monitoring, validation, encryption, backups, and strong security 
including RBAC, JWT/session management, password policies, MFA-ready architecture, 
API authorization, data privacy, audit trails, and secure document access. Define 
complete workflows such as Recruitment → Candidate Selection → Offer → Joining → 
Onboarding → Employee → Attendance/Leave → Payroll → Performance → 
Promotion/Transfer → Offboarding/Exit, with configurable approval chains for HR, 
managers, finance, and admins. Include master-data configuration, organization settings, 
financial/payroll settings, notification templates, workflow configuration, reports, audit logs, 
and system administration. The final system should be production-ready, scalable, API-
driven, well-documented, tested, and include BRD, SRS, database schema/ERD, API 
documentation, RTM, UI/UX specifications, user stories with acceptance criteria, test 
cases, deployment documentation, and complete role-wise functional requirements.
